text:
maya: Heads-up — AcmeHealth wants an Optimize feature that auto-suggests batching + cache configs and fires eval-triggered alerts when quality drops. They need a pilot within 6 weeks to onboard their clinical summarization flow.

alex: Can we scope an MVP? full automation is huge. propose: (1) adaptive batching heuristics + UI recommendations, (2) prefix/KV cache TTL defaults + demo, (3) eval-alert plumbing (signal only, no auto-rollbacks). no quant recs for MVP.

samir: +1 to deferring quant recs. also need a minimal eval set from Acme to tune thresholds. what's the target SLO? p95 vs p99 latency? quality loss tolerances?

maya: They said p95 < 350ms for short prompts, and will tolerate up to 4% regression on our RD metrics before a human review. That gives us a threshold to alert on.

emily: Operational constraints: pilot runs on Dedicated pool with mixed GPUs. batching can't push p99 beyond 600ms. We'll need visibility: per-route token/sec, batch size histograms, eval alert rate.

alex: For implementation plan I can do a lightweight adaptive batch heuristic: start with static batch size tuned by length buckets + online cap by latency budget. Fallback: single-request sync. for caching, expose `cache.prefix_ttl` and `cache.kv_enabled` as toggles. sample quick config below:

```json
{
  "adaptive_batching": {
    "enabled": true,
    "length_buckets": [64, 256, 1024],
    "max_batch_by_bucket": [16, 8, 4],
    "latency_budget_ms": 350
  },
  "cache": {
    "prefix_ttl_seconds": 45,
    "kv_cache_enabled": true
  }
}
```

samir: For eval-alerts: we should hook into existing eval pipeline. signal types: n-gram overlap + model-specific embedding drift + human-labeled sentinel tests. Alert when combined score rises above threshold for 3 consecutive windows (window = 1k requests). Do we have an endpoint for eval triggers?

emily: ops-bot:deploy-check returned that we can add alerting hooks to the metrics ingestion path but we need a small schema change (adds `eval_signal` tag). I'll queue infra change.

ops-bot: infra-ticket created: #INF-5123 add eval_signal tag to metrics ingestion. ETA 5d.

julian: Negotiation note: product asks for 6-week pilot but engineering estimates 8-9 weeks if we include instrumentation and customer eval set collection. Can we compress scope?

maya: Let's compress: aim for a 6-week MLP that includes adaptive batching + basic cache toggles + read-only eval alerts (signals in console). Defer: UI recommendations, multi-model quant recs, and auto rollback. If we hit blockers, push to a second 4-week phase.

alex: That works. Need two things from Acme: (A) sample traffic profile + latency targets by route, (B) a 1k labeled eval set or permission to run sentinel queries.

samir: Also request their acceptance criteria in writing: what constitutes "no worse than 4% regression" — which metric(s)? We'll need that to wire alerts correctly.

maya: I'll ask them for `traffic_profile.csv`, `eval_labels.csv`, and sign-off on acceptance metrics. I'll ping their eng lead. @alex will you draft the minimal config UI we'll expose in Console?

alex: I’ll drop a sketch in product design channel today.

emily: I'll reserve a Dedicated pool slice for the pilot and add tracing hooks. ops-bot: create monitoring runbook stub for eval-alert ops.

ops-bot: runbook stub created: #RUN-2107. includes steps: acknowledge alert, run evaluation job, triage to model-owner, disable batching fallback if needed.

maya: Great. Acceptance gates for MVP: 1) adaptive batching live with latency SLOs visible in Console, 2) cache toggles applied and measured for token savings, 3) eval-alerts firing to console with clear signal taxonomy, 4) customer sign-off on no-regression criteria.

julian: Risks: noisy alerts from small eval sets, customer traffic not representative, and quant rec omission might push them to DIY. Mitigation: agree pilot success criteria and limited timeframe for rollouts.

maya: OK — I'll send scope doc + ask for Acme artifacts. If they can only deliver a small eval set we'll run expanded sentinel jobs on their data. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
